page: Microsoft Azure D48ds_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 48 dedicated vCPUs distributed across 24 physical cores with 2 threads per core, supported by a 35 MB L3 cache and AVX-512 vector extensions. The instance is provisioned with 192 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware configuration bundles 1933 GB of local SSD storage, while excluding discrete GPU acceleration.

Benchmark evaluations reveal balanced general compute performance paired with strong memory subsystem throughput. In synthetic CPU assessments, the instance achieved 44,208.53 in multi-core stress-ng tests and 11,691.0 in Geekbench multi-core evaluation, alongside a Clang software compilation score of 29,842.0. Memory benchmarks highlight upper-quartile capability, with PassMark memory scoring in the top 25% at 2,813.21 and uncached read bandwidth reaching 104.44 GB/sec. Conversely, CPU-only large language model text generation metrics rank in the bottom 25%, showing throughput bottlenecks on larger parameter models due to the absence of dedicated accelerators.

The bundled 1933 GB local SSD offers qualitative operational efficiency by delivering low-latency temporary storage without requiring immediately attached persistent volumes for scratch operations. With high multi-threaded compute density, robust memory throughput, and direct local storage, the D48ds_v4 is suited for relational database hosting, in-memory caching platforms such as Redis, continuous integration and build servers, and batch data processing pipelines.
